audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may omit the homebuilder’s core inventory reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 inventory cash-flow increase of $313.465 million plus $57.193 million net joint-venture cash investment equals $370.658 million, 98.3% of the $377.2 million OE anchor; the maintenance portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted maintenance inventory and joint-venture funding would reduce owner earnings and require growth forecasts to consume additional working capital.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, we invested $523.7 million in land acquisitions and $645.6 million in land development.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that land, development and housing inventory require substantial recurring capital, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation deducted a normalized maintenance requirement. Under the base valuation multiple, a sustained OE reduction of only about $28.8 million, or 7.6% of the anchor, would remove the $405.2 million equity-value cushion that places the market price below the stated buy-below price. The unresolved maintenance portion is therefore reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to inventory changes, accounts payable, development accruals, deposits, inventory not owned and net joint-venture funding; separate maintenance from expansion and rerun every scenario with growth-funded incremental working capital.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat all cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $735.941 million added to equity, equal to $27.68 per diluted share and 12.2% of the $6.036 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash classified as operationally required should not be added as a non-operating asset in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to continue managing our balance sheet and liquidity carefully in 2026 by managing our spending on land acquisition and development and construction of inventory homes, as well as overhead expenditures, relative to our ongoing volume of home deliveries, and we expect to meet our current and anticipated cash requirements in 2026 from cash receipts, excess cash balances and availability under our credit facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the entire reported cash balance, although the filing identifies approximately $735.7 million as unrestricted rather than as distributable excess. If more than approximately $405.2 million of the balance is operationally required, the base buy-below price falls below the $148.26 market price. Excluding all cash would reduce base value to about $199.37 per share and the buy-below price to about $139.56.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum homebuilding and mortgage-subsidiary liquidity, seasonal peak funding, covenant and regulatory cash, committed land spending and near-term debt service; add only the documented surplus and rerun the bridge and buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Sold-mortgage guarantees create contingent claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: June 2026 recorded liability of $1.4 million, underwriting inquiries covering $5.1 million of loans, and limited-life guarantees covering $722.1 million of loans; long-duration collectability exposure is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected guarantee, repurchase and indemnity losses reduce financial-services owner earnings; losses exceeding recorded reserves also reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Actual future costs associated with loans guaranteed or indemnified could differ materially from our current estimated amounts.
audit_findings.explanation: The contingent obligations and recorded reserve are demonstrated, but no excess loss is demonstrated. The $1.4 million reserve and $5.1 million inquiry balance are small compared with the $6.036 billion base equity value, while the filing does not quantify the net exposure on five-to-thirty-year collectability guarantees. The record therefore cannot establish whether the unreserved tail is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain guarantee vintages, delinquency and claim performance, repurchase demands, indemnity payments, investor concentrations and gross exposure net of collateral; compare normalized expected losses with charges already included in OE and rerun if under-reserved.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest can evade the equity-OE interest rail
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 interest capitalized of $36.037 million less $30.191 million released to expense produced a $5.846 million pretax deferral, about $4.472 million after tax and 1.2% of the $377.2 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest retained in inventory rather than released through cost of sales can temporarily raise equity-level OE if the inventory investment is not separately deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company capitalizes interest during land development and home construction.
audit_findings.explanation: Capitalization is demonstrated, but the filing also shows capitalized interest being released through cost of sales. The relevant 2025 timing difference was $5.846 million pretax; applying the filed 23.5% tax rate and the base valuation multiple gives approximately $62.8 million of value, $2.36 per share, or $1.65 per share at the 30% margin of safety. That is well below the $10.67 gap between price and the stated buy-below price. Recent net deferrals were also only $2.519 million in 2023 and $3.809 million in 2024.
audit_findings.action: Confirm for every OE year that only portfolio interest income was purged and reconcile interest incurred, capitalized and released; correct any amount beyond the disclosed net timing differences.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor contains unusually large impairment and abandonment charges
audit_findings.magnitude: $47.669 million pretax in 2025, approximately $36.467 million after tax at 23.5%; a full removal would add about $512.3 million, $19.27 per share, or $13.49 per share at the 30% margin of safety
audit_findings.mechanism: An exceptional charge embedded in the latest-actual OE anchor depresses every forecast year and terminal value; a recurring through-cycle allowance must remain.
audit_findings.evidence: We recorded an aggregate charge of $47.7 million during 2025 that included $11.8 million of write-offs of land deposits and pre-acquisition costs for land we no longer intend to purchase and $35.9 million of inventory impairments.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge is demonstrated, but its exceptional portion is unresolved. Filed inventory losses were $9.244 million in 2024 and $10.608 million in 2023, confirming that zero is not an appropriate recurring allowance. Nevertheless, the quantified potential adjustment is large enough to change valuation outputs materially, even though its direction would increase rather than reduce estimated value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the OE anchor contains the charge without adjustment, compile the complete-cycle history of inventory impairments and abandoned deposits, set a recurring allowance, and rerun all scenarios using only the excess over that allowance.

audit_findings.title: A 2025 tax benefit expires during the forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.5 million, 1.2% of the $377.2 million OE anchor; carrying it perpetually adds about $63.2 million to base value, $2.38 per share, or $1.66 per share at the 30% margin of safety
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring tax benefit inflates after-tax anchor OE and therefore forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (the “Act”) enacted on July 4, 2025, terminates the availability of this benefit on June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The expiration is demonstrated, and the stated mechanical growth method does not identify a separate tax normalization. The resulting approximately $63.2 million base-value effect is only 1.0% of the $6.036 billion base equity value and would leave the adjusted buy-below price around $157.27, still above the $148.26 market price.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $4.5 million benefit from normalized annual OE, apply the post-expiration cash tax rate from the second half of 2026 onward, and update the scenario outputs.
